Aindavamāsanirṇaya
jy. by Gaṇeśadatta. Stein 156 (inc.).

Aindavānandanāṭaka
drama in 8 Acts dealing with the story of Yayāti. by Rāmacandra, son of Śrīharṣa of the Guhavaṁśa, patronised by a king of Bengal (Gauḍendra), probably a Muhammadan king belonging to 15th or 16th century. Burnell 167b. TD. 4335 (beg. missing). See Ind. Cult. II. p. 776.

Aindra
śaiva. Upāgamas in Aṁśumat an. Raurava Āgamas. See list in Kāmikā.

Aindragāyatrīmanuvidhāna
mantra. on the procedure to be adopted before reciting the Aindragāyatrī mantra. MT. 5180 (inc.). C.. next.

Aindragāyatrīmantra
MT. 5458 (b) (fol. 5).

Aindragāyatrīhṛdaya
mantra. MD. 16689 (inc.).

Aindrajāla
Kavīndrācārya 2118. See Indrajāla, NCC. II. p.. 250b-251a. [Page090-a.

Aindrajāla
from Mantrasāra of Pārvatīputra Nityanātha. C.. NCC. II. p. 251a an. Kautukaº (Kautūhalaº).

Aindradhvajapūjāvidhāna
Jain. by Viśvabhūṣaṇa, son of Viśālakīrti. MT. 1598. See also NCC. II. p. 252 under Indradhvaja.

Aindranighaṇṭu
lex. in 38 verses. ascribed to Vararuci an. Indra. almost identical with the Ekākṣarakośa of Puruṣottamadeva. See above Ekākṣarakośa ascribed to Vararuci. See also NCC. II. p. 253b.
Burnell 52a. Gough p. 143. IO. i. 296b fn. Mysore I. p. 604. TD. 4738.

Aindramatavāstuśāsra
śilpa. Extracted in MT. 3825 (Paṭala 70).

Aindravyākaraṇa
one of the eight ancient schools of Skt. gr. according to tradition (see indrazcandraH etc. Intro. verse 2, Mugdhabodha, an. also Śākaṭ. vyā. I. ii. 37); for ref. s to Indra an. language-study, see Taitt. Saṁ. VI. 4. 7, Mahābhāṣya I. 1. 1. For a. account of Aindra a. a pre-Pāṇinian school, studied first by Kātyāyana-Vararuci, Vyāḍi an. Indradatta an. later superseded by Pāṇini's, see Kathāsaritsāgara I. 4. 25.
For a detailed study of Aindra an. its history, see A. C. Burnell ‘On the Aindra School of Grammarians’. Survives in Prātiśākhyas, Kātantra, Pāli an. Tamil (Tolkāppiyam, the oldest Tamil gr. is described a. based on it). However Aindra or Indra not q. by Yāska, Pāṇini, Kātyāyana or Patañjali, the only quotation being in Jñānavimala's C. on Maheśvara's Śabdaprakāśa, where ‘Siddhir anuktānām rūḍheh2’ is said to be its opening sūtra (See Peters. II. p. 65); but this sūtra is not found in Kātantra or Jainendra. Śākaṭ. vyā. I. 2. 37 mentions Indra (Ind. [Page090-b] Ant. XVI. p. 27); Udayaprabhasūri, in his Upadeśamālākarṇikā (Ind. Ant. X. p. 79) gives a tradition on Jainendra vyā. being Aindra.
See NCC. II. p.. 249b, 250a; S. K. Belvalkar, Systems of Skt. Gr. p.. 10-12; RASB. VI. Preface xlviii. Also Poona Ori. XX. 1955. p.. 31-40. Kavindrācārya 145.
